posts.body:
Hi, I'm hoping that someone may be able to come up with an amazing idea for me as I'm really struggling to think of something good!

Some friends and I who all have babies of a similar age have decided to do a kind of secret santa for their first birthday presents with a price limit of £20 so I'm trying to think of something lovely for the baby girl I've picked.

I don't want to do clothes as not hugely exciting and couldn't guarantee sizing, her parents are quite traditional and don't like plasticky, noisy/light up toys (maybe something wooden could be a possibility though?), obviously nothing too big as would be a bit rude to take over their house, and can't really do books as got them for the last 2 occasions within the group so need to do something a bit different this time really.

Any help would be much appreciated. I really want to get something she'll love.

Thanks ☺

If you haven’t already, join the forum to reply! [purplesignup][/purplesignup]

posts.body: An independent toy shop is great for this kind of thing. Wooden O rings are great, as are those puzzles where you put the animals in the right shaped hole (good for parents teaching their child tge different animals) or a wooden pull along toy like a cow fir when they start walking. Just find a small independent toy shop and they'll have lots of options.

posts.body:
I always get wooden push along toys for one-year-olds and they go down very well with the children and the parents. They're the wooden toys with an animal on wheels at the bottom of a wooden pole. The wheels often have wooden beads on strings attached so they make a pleasant clunking sound as they're pushed.

i realise they look like the sorts of toys that parents like and kids ignore but genuinely they've been a hit every time and I've given them to around 10 one-year-olds now. Often available in independent toy shops too

posts.body:
I completely agree! I love my family very much but if I get another giant teddy bear for the kids at Christmas, it will be starting the new year in a charity shop window! 

My sister in law bought my son one last year - he smiled at it once and since then it has been stuffed in a wardrobe. Told my mum it would be shopped before we moved into the house and she told me that I needed to take it to the new house and put it in one of the kids bedrooms so my sister in law can see it when they come for a nosey at new house...

Then I am allowed to throw it away.

I'm 31 and my mum still tells me what to do. :rotfl:
